Archive item 2: EPA Victoria – Compliance Notice No. 2024-1187 (Site 7, 14-22 Dune Road)
Source format: EPA compliance notice

The site is a scheduled premises under item 32 of Schedule 1 of the *Environment Protection Regulations 2021* (Vic) (ammonia refrigeration, quantity threshold exceeded). The premises holds EPA licence No. L-2024-0417-AM, current to 30 June 2026.

On 14, 15 and 16 October 2024, Authorised Officers Marek and Nguyen attended the site to conduct a routine compliance inspection under section 170 of the Act. The inspection included a review of the site's environmental management system, ammonia inventory records, maintenance logs, and a physical inspection of the refrigeration plant, including all units in the engine room and the external evaporative condensers.

---

**2. INSPECTION FINDINGS**

The inspection identified a number of matters requiring attention. These are set out below, grouped by area of concern. The Company should note that the matters identified are not intended to be an exhaustive list of non-compliances at the site, and the EPA may take further action in relation to any matters identified during this or any subsequent inspection.

**2.1 Refrigeration Unit RU-104 – Ammonia Refrigeration Unit**

Refrigeration Unit RU-104 (unit serial no. 2017-AL-104, manufacturer: Sabroe, model no. SAB 163L) is a screw compressor unit located in the engine room. The unit serves the high-temperature (chiller) circuit serving cold rooms 1–4 and the main packing area.

The inspection found that RU-104 is operating with a known and documented loss of ammonia refrigerant to atmosphere. The EPA notice states Refrigeration Unit RU-104 compliance_status is requires_retrofit. Record status: current. In particular, the unit's shaft seal assembly is leaking, and the unit has been operating in this condition since at least September 2024. The Company's maintenance records indicate that a temporary repair was attempted on 12 September 2024, but the leak has persisted.

The EPA considers that the ongoing operation of RU-104 without a permanent retrofit of the shaft seal and associated piping constitutes a failure to comply with the general environmental duty under section 25 of the Act, and with the licence condition LC-04 (maintenance of plant to minimise risk of emissions). The Company is required to carry out a permanent retrofit of RU-104, as detailed in Section 4 below.

**2.2 Ammonia Inventory and Mass Balance Records**

The Company's ammonia inventory log for the period July–October 2024 was reviewed. The log records refrigerant added to the system on the following dates:

- 3 July 2024 – 45 kg added to RU-104 circuit
- 18 August 2024 – 30 kg added to RU-104 circuit
- 12 September 2024 – 60 kg added to RU-104 circuit (recorded as "temporary repair top-up")

The total refrigerant added over the period (135 kg) is significantly higher than the site's historical average of approximately 20 kg per quarter. The EPA considers this to be consistent with a persistent leak in the RU-104 circuit. The Company's mass balance calculations for the quarter ending 30 September 2024 were not available at the time of inspection; these are required to be submitted under licence condition LC-07.

**2.3 Bunding and Containment**

The secondary containment bunding around the RU-104 unit was inspected. The bund wall on the eastern side of the unit was found to be in poor condition, with a visible crack approximately 400 mm long and 5 mm wide, running vertically from the top of the wall. The crack appears to have been present for some time, as evidenced by staining and salt deposits. The bund wall does not currently meet the requirements of AS 3780-2008 (The storage and handling of corrosive substances) in that it is not impermeable to the stored substance.

This notice amends the Environment Protection Act 2017 (the Act) compliance notice issued to Port Phillip Cold Storage Pty Ltd (the Operator) on 5 November 2024. The reason for this amendment is that the Operator has provided evidence, dated 7 November 2024, of a contractual delay in the delivery of the required ammonia sensors from the supplier. The EPA accepts that the delay is outside the Operator's reasonable control. All other requirements of clause 7.2, including the system's alarm set points, siting, and certification requirements, remain unchanged.

documents.title: EPA Victoria – Compliance Notice No. 2024-1187 (Site 7, 14-22 Dune Road)
documents.content:
The site is a scheduled premises under item 32 of Schedule 1 of the *Environment Protection Regulations 2021* (Vic) (ammonia refrigeration, quantity threshold exceeded). The premises holds EPA licence No. L-2024-0417-AM, current to 30 June 2026.

On 14, 15 and 16 October 2024, Authorised Officers Marek and Nguyen attended the site to conduct a routine compliance inspection under section 170 of the Act. The inspection included a review of the site's environmental management system, ammonia inventory records, maintenance logs, and a physical inspection of the refrigeration plant, including all units in the engine room and the external evaporative condensers.

---

**2. INSPECTION FINDINGS**

The inspection identified a number of matters requiring attention. These are set out below, grouped by area of concern. The Company should note that the matters identified are not intended to be an exhaustive list of non-compliances at the site, and the EPA may take further action in relation to any matters identified during this or any subsequent inspection.

**2.1 Refrigeration Unit RU-104 – Ammonia Refrigeration Unit**

Refrigeration Unit RU-104 (unit serial no. 2017-AL-104, manufacturer: Sabroe, model no. SAB 163L) is a screw compressor unit located in the engine room. The unit serves the high-temperature (chiller) circuit serving cold rooms 1–4 and the main packing area.

The inspection found that RU-104 is operating with a known and documented loss of ammonia refrigerant to atmosphere. The EPA notice states Refrigeration Unit RU-104 compliance_status is requires_retrofit. Record status: current. In particular, the unit's shaft seal assembly is leaking, and the unit has been operating in this condition since at least September 2024. The Company's maintenance records indicate that a temporary repair was attempted on 12 September 2024, but the leak has persisted.

The EPA considers that the ongoing operation of RU-104 without a permanent retrofit of the shaft seal and associated piping constitutes a failure to comply with the general environmental duty under section 25 of the Act, and with the licence condition LC-04 (maintenance of plant to minimise risk of emissions). The Company is required to carry out a permanent retrofit of RU-104, as detailed in Section 4 below.

**2.2 Ammonia Inventory and Mass Balance Records**

The Company's ammonia inventory log for the period July–October 2024 was reviewed. The log records refrigerant added to the system on the following dates:

- 3 July 2024 – 45 kg added to RU-104 circuit
- 18 August 2024 – 30 kg added to RU-104 circuit
- 12 September 2024 – 60 kg added to RU-104 circuit (recorded as "temporary repair top-up")

The total refrigerant added over the period (135 kg) is significantly higher than the site's historical average of approximately 20 kg per quarter. The EPA considers this to be consistent with a persistent leak in the RU-104 circuit. The Company's mass balance calculations for the quarter ending 30 September 2024 were not available at the time of inspection; these are required to be submitted under licence condition LC-07.

**2.3 Bunding and Containment**

The secondary containment bunding around the RU-104 unit was inspected. The bund wall on the eastern side of the unit was found to be in poor condition, with a visible crack approximately 400 mm long and 5 mm wide, running vertically from the top of the wall. The crack appears to have been present for some time, as evidenced by staining and salt deposits. The bund wall does not currently meet the requirements of AS 3780-2008 (The storage and handling of corrosive substances) in that it is not impermeable to the stored substance.

**EPA VICTORIA**
Compliance Notice No. 2024-1187
Site 7, 14-22 Dune Road, Geelong

**Issued under section 31B of the Environment Protection Act 2017**

---

**3. REQUIRED ACTIONS**

The Company is required to undertake the following actions. All actions must be completed by the dates specified. The EPA may vary, extend or revoke these requirements in writing at any time. Nothing in this notice limits the EPA's ability to take other enforcement action, including the issue of an infringement notice or a prosecution, in relation to the contraventions described in this notice.

**3.1 Permanent Retrofit of Refrigeration Unit RU-104**

The EPA notice sets Refrigeration Unit RU-104 retrofit_deadline as 2025-06-30. Record status: current. This is the date by which all actions required under this clause must be completed and verified, and the EPA must be notified in writing of the completion of the retrofit works.

By no later than **4:00 pm on 2025-06-30**, the Company must:

(a) Engage a suitably qualified refrigeration engineer (holding at least a Certificate III in Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, or equivalent) to design a permanent retrofit of the shaft seal assembly and the associated piping on RU-104. The design must be consistent with AS/NZS 5149.1:2016 and the manufacturer's original equipment specifications, or a documented engineering justification for any deviation.

(b) Carry out the permanent retrofit works, which must include:

(i) replacement of the existing shaft seal with a double mechanical seal of a type approved by the unit manufacturer, complete with an intermediate chamber fitted with a pressure switch and a vent to a safe location;

(ii) replacement of all flexible hoses in the RU-104 circuit with hard-drawn copper or stainless steel piping, or with flexible hoses that meet the requirements of AS 3961-2017 and are rated for ammonia service;

(iii) installation of a permanent leak detection system on the RU-104 circuit, capable of detecting ammonia concentrations of 25 ppm or lower and providing an audible and visible alarm at a continuously manned location; and

(iv) pressure testing of the repaired circuit to 1.1 times the maximum allowable working pressure, followed by a full system evacuation and re-commissioning in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and AS/NZS 5149.1:2016.

(c) Provide to the EPA, within 14 days of completion of the retrofit works, a report prepared by the refrigeration engineer who supervised the works. The report must include:

(i) a description of the works undertaken, including photographs of the completed installation;

(ii) confirmation that the works were carried out in accordance with the design referred to in paragraph (a), or a description of any variation and the reason for it;

(iii) the results of the pressure test and leak detection system commissioning tests; and

(iv) a signed statement that the unit is, to the best of the engineer's knowledge and belief, free from refrigerant leaks.

**3.2 Interim Measures Pending Retrofit**

Until the retrofit works under clause 3.1 are completed, the Company must:

(a) continue to operate RU-104 only with a functioning refrigerant leak detection system capable of detecting a leak of 25 ppm or greater, and record the readings of that system at least once per shift in the site log;

(b) carry out a weekly visual inspection of the RU-104 shaft seal area, the bund wall, and all accessible pipework in the RU-104 circuit, and record the results of each inspection in the site log, including any odour observations;

**RE: AMENDMENT OF COMPLIANCE NOTICE NO. 2024-1187 – ISSUED 5 NOVEMBER 2024**

This notice amends the Environment Protection Act 2017 (the Act) compliance notice issued to Port Phillip Cold Storage Pty Ltd (the Operator) on 5 November 2024. Except as expressly amended below, all terms, conditions, obligations, and schedules of the original notice remain in force and are binding on the Operator.

This amendment is issued following the Operator's written request dated 8 November 2024, and further to EPA site inspection records of 4 November 2024. The EPA is satisfied that the amendment does not reduce the overall level of environmental protection required at the Site, and that the revised compliance dates remain consistent with the risk posed by the operation.

**1. AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 7.2 – REFRIGERANT LEAK DETECTION SYSTEM**

Clause 7.2 of the original notice is amended by deleting the words "a continuous refrigerant leak detection system shall be installed and fully operational at the Site no later than 1700 hours on 15 November 2024" and substituting the following:

"a continuous refrigerant leak detection system shall be installed and fully operational at the Site no later than 1700 hours on 22 November 2024."

The reason for this amendment is that the Operator has provided evidence, dated 7 November 2024, of a contractual delay in the delivery of the required ammonia sensors from the supplier. The EPA accepts that the delay is outside the Operator's reasonable control. All other requirements of clause 7.2, including the system's alarm set points, siting, and certification requirements, remain unchanged.

**2. AMENDMENT TO SCHEDULE 2 – MONITORING AND REPORTING**

Schedule 2, item 4, is amended by adding the following row after the existing row for "Monthly ammonia mass balance report":

| Item | Requirement | Frequency | Due date |
|------|-------------|-----------|----------|
| 4A | Quarterly fugitive emissions scan using optical gas imaging (OGI) camera, undertaken by a suitably qualified contractor. The scan must cover all flanges, valves, and pump seals on the high-stage and low-stage refrigerant circuits. A report of the scan, including images and a statement of any leaks found, must be submitted to the EPA. | Quarterly | First report due by 14 February 2025, and thereafter within 14 days of the end of each quarter. |

This amendment is made to address the EPA's finding, recorded in the inspection report of 4 November 2024, that the existing fixed-point detection arrangement may not fully cover all potential leak points in the plant room. The OGI scan is a supplementary measure and does not replace any obligation under clause 7.2.

**3. CORRECTION TO CLAUSE 3.1 – DEFINITION OF "STORAGE SPECIFICATION"**

For the avoidance of doubt, the EPA notes that the definition of **Storage specification** in clause 3.1 is corrected to read as follows:

**Storage specification** means the documented temperature, humidity, and handling requirements for a product, as provided by the customer or manufacturer, and includes any revision to those requirements that is communicated to the Operator in writing before the product is received at the Site.
